Estimate constant or time-varying point spread functions

Source: R/estimate_psf.R
estimate_psf.Rd

Estimate a log-concave PSF from a calibration standard or an overlapping sample, and construct its sparse scan-by-scan convolution design. Numeric retention-time names and the bundled data's alkanes_TIC attributes are recognised automatically.

Usage

estimate_psf(
  y,
  family = quasipoisson("identity"),
  time = NULL,
  standard = attr(y, "alkanes_TIC"),
  method = c("auto", "standard", "blind"),
  nwindows = 1L,
  precluster = 1L,
  dispersion = NULL,
  theta = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  ncores = NULL,
  control = list(),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

y

Numeric signal vector, scan-by-channel matrix, or a list with Y and time. Sparse matrices are accepted. At least nine scans are needed.

family

Identity-link family supported by splogconNMF(), including Gaussian, Poisson, quasipoisson, negative binomial, nb1(), ordinary Gamma_censored() and common-scale Gamma_scale(). Character names are also accepted. Gaussian observations may be negative.

time

Increasing sample retention times. Defaults to numeric names or row names, or scan indices when names are absent. The standard and sample must use the same time units.

standard

Optional nonoverlapping calibration signal, with its own retention-time names or list(Y=..., time=...). Defaults to attr(y, "alkanes_TIC"), supplied with GCMS_data1 and GCMS_data2.

method

"auto" calibrates from an available standard and then refines on the sample; without a standard it uses blind sample estimation. "standard" uses calibration alone, treating y as the standard when standard=NULL. "blind" estimates directly from the overlapping sample. A supplied control$kernel_est takes precedence over automatic calibration.

nwindows

Number of PSF anchors across the sample. 1L gives a constant PSF. Multiple anchors are smoothly interpolated on the log-profile scale.

precluster

FALSE retains the original channels, 1L sums all channels, and an integer requests that many outcome groups at most. TRUE uses at most 32 groups. The default uses the total-ion signal. Poisson distances use channel totals as size factors and native OpenMP Ward or Bregman clustering; see glm_cluster().

dispersion, theta

Shared noise parameters, as in splogconNMF(). Omitted parameters are estimated from temporal differences and held fixed during PSF estimation. For NB2, theta is the shape parameter.

weights, offset

Nonnegative scalar, scan vector or matrix matching the signal used for estimation. In method="standard" these refer to the standard; in "auto" and "blind" they refer to the sample. An identity-link offset is an additive known signal. Grouped offsets are summed.

ncores

Number of native threads; defaults to the physical core count.

control

Named list. L fixes an odd kernel length; otherwise standard support is inferred from its fitted peak masses and blind support defaults to 41 scans. kernel_est supplies a vector or one kernel row per window. maxiter=8L and tol=1e-3 control blind iterations; maxiter=0L returns the supplied kernel design directly. fit is a named list of additional L0glm_blind_deco() fitting options, such as IC or relaxed. Standard controls include n_peaks=NULL, baseline_df=NULL, baseline_tau=0.05, peak_snr=5, peak_height=NULL, peak_min_distance=NULL, support_fraction=0.005, psf_mass=0.999 and support_quantile=0.95. linkage="ward" controls channel clustering. censor=0.5 is the Gamma detection limit, taken from a supplied scalar family constructor unless explicitly overridden.

verbose

Print the estimation mode, aggregation and fitted PSF width.

Value

A list containing the sparse design X (X_spikes), kernel vector or matrix g_hat, psf_kernels, relative-time psf_offsets, anchor retention times psf_timepoints, sample time, fitted width_scans, method, noise spec, Gamma detection limit censor, aggregation diagnostics, optional calibration, blind windows, iterations, converged and elapsed seconds. The result can be passed directly as X=psf$X to splogconNMF() or L0glm.fit(). No observed matrix is retained.

Details

Standard calibration. A lower-quantile spline estimates background. Isolated calibration peaks are retained using signal-to-noise and profile geometry. Each peak is fitted on its original observation scale: $$\mu_{ij}=b_{ij}+o_{ij}+h_i s_j,\qquad h_i>0,\quad \Delta^2\log h_i\leq0.$$ Native likelihood-based profile updates minimize \(-\sum_{ij}w_{ij}\ell(y_{ij};\mu_{ij})\) while imposing hard log concavity. The logarithm parameterizes the positive profile; likelihood or quasi-likelihood is evaluated on the original observation scale. Unit-area kernels are aligned by their centroid and resampled to the sample scan interval. Isolated-peak fitting, automatic support and interpolation share helpers with estimate_psf_from_std().

Blind refinement. L0glm_blind_deco() alternates sparse nonnegative spike fitting with PSF estimation. Completed candidates are compared using the requested information criterion and the best checkpoint is retained. The unpenalized background and any known offset enter both updates. With fixed-dispersion quasipoisson counts, the Poisson likelihood weighted by \(1/\phi\) has the same mean-dependent objective. This permits the native Poisson backend while preserving the quasipoisson noise scale. For multiple windows, local kernels are estimated independently, and \(\log g_t=(1-a)\log g_l+a\log g_r\), with smoothstep weights \(a=u^2(3-2u)\), joins adjacent anchors. The returned design has nonnegative, unit-sum, log-concave columns, including truncated boundary columns. Kernel vectors are indexed by scans. Standard profiles are resampled using the median sample scan interval; a constant kernel gives shifted copies on that scan grid, independently of rounding in the retention-time labels.

Channel aggregation. Poisson sums retain their model. Shared-dispersion quasipoisson and NB1 sums retain their mean-variance relationship, Gaussian variances add, and common-scale Gamma shapes add. NB2 and ordinary Gamma use variance matching with observed channel fractions \(r_j=\sum_i y_{ij}/\sum_{i,j\in G}y_{ij}\): $$\theta_G=\theta/\sum_{j\in G}r_j^2,\qquad \phi_G=\phi\sum_{j\in G}r_j^2.$$ These are generally moment-matched sum distributions. Equal component means give exact NB2 or ordinary Gamma closure under shared per-channel parameters. Varying channel proportions over time also affect the variance approximation. Censored Gamma aggregation is approximate and flagged separately. Different observation weights within a group are averaged and flagged in the returned diagnostics; retain the original channels for exact weighted fitting.

Calibration and sample peaks should represent the same chromatographic conditions. Broad overloaded standard peaks can require sample refinement; method="standard" keeps the calibration unchanged. Supplied kernels are useful when a particular experimental PSF is already known.

References

de Rooi, J. J. and Eilers, P. H. C. (2011). Deconvolution of pulse trains with the L0 penalty. Analytica Chimica Acta 705, 218–226. doi:10.1016/j.aca.2011.05.030 .

See also

GCMSdeco(), L0glm_blind_deco(), estimate_psf_from_std(), splogconNMF(), glm_cluster()

Examples

set.seed(12)
n <- 300L
time <- seq_len(n) / 60
kernel <- dnorm(-15:15, sd = 2.5)
kernel <- kernel / sum(kernel)
A <- matrix(0, n, 3L)
A[c(40, 120, 210, 270), ] <- 30000
mu <- as.matrix(convmatrix(kernel, n) %*% A) + 10
Y <- matrix(rpois(length(mu), mu), n, 3L)
rownames(Y) <- time

# Isolated standard peaks provide a PSF on the sample's retention-time grid.
calibration <- estimate_psf(Y, standard = list(Y = Y, time = time),
  method = "standard", nwindows = 3L, ncores = 2L)
dim(calibration$X)
Matrix::colSums(calibration$X)[1:5]
matplot(calibration$psf_offsets, t(calibration$psf_kernels),
  type = "l", lty = 1, xlab = "Relative retention time (min)", ylab = "PSF")

# Blind refinement can use the original channels or their grouped sums.
blind <- estimate_psf(Y, standard = NULL, method = "blind", precluster = 2L,
  ncores = 2L, control = list(kernel_est = kernel, maxiter = 2L))
blind$width_scans

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(GCMS_data2)
Y <- GCMS_data2
# The alkane TIC and its time axis are taken from attr(Y, "alkanes_TIC").
psf <- estimate_psf(Y, nwindows = 3L)
B <- splines::bs(as.numeric(rownames(Y)), df = 4L, intercept = TRUE)
fit <- splogconNMF(psf$X, Y, background = B,
  family = quasipoisson("identity"), precluster = 32L)

# Calibration alone, or a single common PSF, are available through the same API.
calibrated <- estimate_psf(Y, method = "standard", nwindows = 3L)
constant <- estimate_psf(Y, nwindows = 1L)
} # }
